sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova: A New Generation of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: December 3, 2024 announcement expressly says Nova Micro, Lite and Pro are generally available that day. Identifies Amazon as developer and Nova as the family, with Lite accepting text, image and video and producing text.

sources.title: Nova Lite - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Exact amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 card still identifies Nova Lite with 300K context, text/image/video input, text output and client-side tool calling. It has no total or active parameter specification. Its December 5, 2024 launch date conflicts with the contemporaneous December 3 GA announcement.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the original publisher PDF on October 27 and extracted its full text; also read the arXiv HTML version. Section 1.1, page 3 explicitly identifies Pro, Lite and Micro as Transformer-based, describes pretraining followed by SFT and preference optimization, and identifies no differently named base with a published size. The report and comparison tables give no nominal total or active parameter count, or dense/MoE topology.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the April 30, 2025 addendum PDF on October 27. It presents Premier as a teacher for customized Pro, Lite and Micro students; that distillation relationship does not establish equal size. Its later comparison tables contain benchmark results, with no Lite total/active parameter specification or dense/MoE disclosure.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Reopened the December 2, 2025 publisher PDF on October 27. Nova 1 Lite appears in core-capability, agentic, multimodal and responsible-AI comparison tables; none has a total or activated-parameter column. API sampling parameters elsewhere in the report are not model parameter counts. Nova 2 specifications do not establish Nova 1 Lite size.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier - AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Service card scoped to April 30, 2025 identifies Lite's multimodal inputs and Transformer-based inference and describes teacher/student customization across the family. It provides no total/active count or sized named-base relationship.

sources.title: Customize Amazon Nova in Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: July 16, 2025 announcement expressly calls Nova a proprietary model family and names Micro, Lite and Pro as the models covered by its customization offering.

sources.title: Available foundation models - Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Inventory dated July 29, 2026 lists Nova Lite (nova-textgeneration-lite) with license AWS Service Terms. The row appears under an Open-Weight Models heading, conflicting with Nova-specific proprietary classification and escrow documentation; the broad heading alone is not treated as a weight-release announcement.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. March 18, 2026 migration guide maps Nova 1 Lite to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0, and its comparison table gives 300K context, text/image/video inputs and Extended Thinking = No. The specifications table has no total or activated-parameter row; Nova 2 is a separately identified successor.

sources.title: Iterative Training - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current documentation explicitly states Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow buckets in AWS-managed accounts instead of being copied into the customer's account. Examples use Nova 2; this corroborates the exact first-generation classification in s7 rather than independently identifying Lite v1.

sources.title: Models.dev Nova Lite v1 source record
sources.evidence: Followed the baseline link. It identifies its metadata as carried over from the OpenRouter provider catalog; it is a discovery source, not primary verification of model specifications.

sources.title: Complete request schema - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current Nova user-guide schema explicitly labels reasoningConfig as applicable to Nova Pro and Nova Lite, with enabled/disabled and low/medium/high effort. This conflicts with the March 2026 exact Nova 1 Lite migration table. The schema does not include an exact Lite API identifier.

sources.title: Using the Converse API - Amazon Nova Version 1
sources.evidence: Page explicitly labels itself Version 1, maps Nova Lite to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0, and documents function calling and image/video inputs. It describes topK but no reasoningConfig or extended-thinking capability; absence here does not by itself prove unsupported reasoning.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Version 1 model specifications
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Version 1 model specifications map Lite to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 and list PDF document support, but no total or active parameter count. The migration guide states document input remains Converse-only.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. Amazon AGI-authored paper, Table 1 on PDF page 6, explicitly has a Params column: Nova Lite is NP, with 300k context and 12/24 release. It supplies no numeric count and has no separate active/activated-parameter column. The table does not expand NP; no numeric interpretation is assigned.

sources.title: PHLoRA: data-free Post-hoc Low-Rank Adapter extraction from full-rank checkpoint
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. This Amazon-hosted paper evaluates Micro, Lite and Pro and exposes attention_qkv, attention_dense, mlp_fc1 and mlp_fc2 adapter target names. Tables 3-6 report benchmark scores, ranks and preserved energy, not model parameter sizes. Ranks 32/64/512 are adapter ranks and do not establish total/active counts or dense topology for Lite.

sources.title: Continued pre-training (CPT) on Nova 2.0 on SageMaker HyperPod
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. AWS explicitly calls Nova Lite 2.0 a larger model than Nova Lite 1.0, while saying it has faster inference. This is evidence against assuming unchanged parameter size across the Lite generations; it gives neither generation a numeric total or active count.

sources.title: Fine-tune Nova 1.0 - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Freshly checked October 27. The run-configuration comparison table maps amazon.nova-lite-v1:0:300k to base model path nova-lite/prod. Full-rank/LoRA settings and instance-count tables give no model parameter sizes and identify no separately sized base. Hardware replicas and adapter configuration are not nominal total/active counts.

name.note: Retain the display name for official Nova Lite / Nova 1 Lite, mapped to amazon.nova-lite-v1:0; this is not Nova 2 Lite.

developer.note: Amazon's launch and its AGI-authored technical report establish developer identity.

family.note: Normalize to the developer's Nova family; Lite is a member/tier rather than a separate family.

release_date.note: Use earliest explicit public GA on December 3. The current Bedrock card's December 5 launch date is retained as a source conflict, not substituted for the contemporaneous release.

open_weights.note: Developer explicitly calls the exact first-generation family proprietary; current Nova docs explain proprietary weights remain in AWS escrow. JumpStart's broad Open-Weight heading conflicts, but its Lite row provides no downloadable checkpoint or self-hosting route.

license.note: Exact Nova Lite row labels its license AWS Service Terms. These are proprietary service/model-use terms, not an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no developer-published nominal total for exact Lite v1. Original and later Nova reports, current v1 specifications and training docs have no numeric size; Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents Table 1 lists Params=NP. No named base with a published count supports inference. Nova Lite 2.0 is explicitly larger than 1.0, and Premier distillation does not imply equal size.

active_parameters_b.note: Freshly checked total and active counts separately, including later Nova 2/MASSIVE-Agents and current training/migration comparison tables. No activated-parameter column or numeric active count for Lite v1 was found. Transformer architecture and adapter target names do not establish dense/MoE topology or an active count; no total-to-active equality is assumed.

architecture.note: The original report explicitly says Transformer-based. This records only that disclosed architecture class; dense versus MoE remains undisclosed.

context_window.note: Both the exact Bedrock card and later Nova 1 Lite comparison specify 300K tokens.

modalities.note: Exact card confirms text/image/video to text. Version 1 specifications add PDF document input; document support is through Converse rather than Invoke.

reasoning.note: Unresolved first-party conflict: the March 2026 Nova 1 Lite comparison says Extended Thinking = No, but the current shared request schema expressly assigns reasoningConfig to Nova Lite. The exact v1 Converse page documents no reasoning mode. No endpoint invocation or version-specific update resolves this; clear baseline false rather than claim either value.

tool_call.note: Client-side tool calling is expressly supported; absence of Nova 2 built-in tools does not negate function calling.

description.value: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
description.note: Summary of documented inputs, output, context and tool calling without speed or price claims.

patch.description: Nova model with text, image, video and PDF input, text output, a 300K-token context and tool calling.
patch.notes: Public GA was announced December 3, 2024; the later Bedrock card lists December 5. Transformer-based is disclosed; total/active counts and dense/MoE topology remain undisclosed. Amazon AGI lists Lite parameters as NP; Nova 2 Lite is explicitly a larger model, so its size cannot be transferred to Lite v1. AWS Service Terms are proprietary use terms; Nova-specific documentation identifies proprietary weights held in AWS-managed escrow despite the JumpStart inventory's broad Open-Weight heading. Reasoning mode is unresolved: the Nova 1 Lite migration table says no extended thinking, while the current shared Nova request schema assigns reasoningConfig to Lite. PDF input is supported through the Converse API.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after reopening original Nova, Premier and Nova 2 reports, exact v1 model specifications, service card and migration tables. New evidence includes Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents Params=NP, PHLoRA adapter tables, v1 training/base-path documentation and AWS disclosure that Nova Lite 2.0 is larger than 1.0. No nominal count, active-count disclosure or sized named-base lineage was found. Preserve the prior release-date, family, architecture, license, modalities and other field decisions, including unresolved reasoning conflict.
